catalog_quote: Perceived stress patterns based on the hundreds of tokens elicited from all nine speakers are clear and consistent. Disyllabic non-verbs (nouns, adjectives, and numerals) are stressed on the second syllable (σ2), and disyllabic verbs are stressed on the first syllable (σ1). ... The σ2 stress perceived on nouns, adjectives, and numerals pertains regardless of morphological composition, as illustrated below. Exceptions are presented in section 4.1.6. ... Stress falls on this σ2 suffix even though it is an open, light syllable and contributes no meaning or function. ... In contrast to nouns, adjectives, and numerals, verbs are never stressed on σ2. Regardless of their morphological composition, they are stressed on σ1. The most explicit evidence of this contrast is illustrated by minimal pairs ... for instance ... the minimal pair [tʰaq.'pa] thag.pa 'rope' vs. ['tʰaq.pa] 'thag.pa 'to grind…

audit.reasoning: The classification (morphological: stress placed by lexical category, σ2 on disyllabic non-verbs incl. light open formative suffixes, σ1 on verbs, noun-verb minimal pairs) rests on a dedicated 2016 open-access instrumental study of Balti stress, which we hold as PDF and text; every fragment of the deciding quotation was confirmed verbatim at the cited sections (4, 4.1, 4.1.1, 4.2, 4.2.1). The secondary Read 1934 'equal emphasis' statement is also present in the held scanned. Nothing in Glottolog's descriptive bibliography (general grammars/sketches 1934-2014, Sprigg 2007 on orthography) or in Caplow's own literature review outranks this source for stress; the only caveat already recorded in the prule is that the study analyses disyllables only. Wishlist items are low priority cross-checks (Caplow 2009 dissertation, LTBA 2016 companion, Bielmeier 1985, Sprigg 1966); none could be fetched sources open
